facts.fact: Under FCC rules, telemarketing calls to a home are prohibited before 8 a.m. and after 9 p.m.
facts.quote: Telemarketing calls to your home are prohibited before 8 a.m. and after 9 p.m., and telemarketers must comply immediately with any do-not-call request you make during a call.

facts.fact: Most mobile carriers let consumers block spam text messages by forwarding the message to 7726 (SPAM), according to the FCC page.
facts.quote: Most mobile carriers let you block spam by forwarding the message to 7726 (SPAM)—check with your provider.

facts.fact: FCC rules require a caller to obtain prior written consent, on paper or through electronic means, before making a prerecorded telemarketing call to a home or wireless phone number.
facts.quote: FCC rules require a caller to obtain your prior written consent – on paper or through electronic means, including website forms or a telephone keypress – before they make a prerecorded telemarketing call

facts.fact: Prerecorded telemarketing calls must provide an opt-out option at the start of the message.
facts.value: at the start of the message
facts.quote: Prerecorded telemarketing calls must provide an opt-out option at the start of the message.

facts.fact: Consumers may opt out of any robocall or robotext at any time and in any reasonable manner, even if they previously gave consent.
facts.quote: You may opt out of any robocall or robotext at any time and in any reasonable manner, even if you previously gave consent for such calls.

facts.fact: All prerecorded voice message calls must include the caller's name, number, and business name at the beginning of the message.
facts.quote: All prerecorded voice message calls must include the caller's name, number, and business name at the beginning of the message.

facts.fact: AI-generated voice calls are illegal unless the consumer has agreed to receive them or the caller is exempt.
facts.quote: AI-generated voice calls are illegal unless the consumer has agreed to receive them or the caller is exempt.

facts.fact: FCC rules ban text messages sent to a mobile phone using an autodialer unless the phone owner previously gave consent or the message is for emergency purposes.
facts.quote: FCC rules ban text messages sent to a mobile phone using an autodialer unless the phone owner previously gave consent to receive the message or the message is sent for emergency purposes.

facts.fact: Commercial texts require written consent, while informational texts may be sent with oral consent.
facts.value: written consent for commercial texts; oral consent for informational texts
facts.quote: Commercial texts require written consent; for informational texts, your consent may be oral.

facts.fact: FCC robotext rules apply even if a consumer has not placed their mobile number on the National Do Not Call Registry.
facts.quote: FCC rules apply even if you have not placed your mobile phone number on the National Do Not Call Registry.

facts.fact: Political robocalls to landlines (autodialed or prerecorded) are allowed without prior consent.
facts.quote: Landlines: Political robocalls (autodialed or prerecorded) are allowed without prior consent.

facts.fact: Political calls, texts, or prerecorded messages to cell phones require the recipient's prior permission unless sent manually.
facts.quote: Cell phones: Political calls, texts, or prerecorded messages require the recipient’s prior permission—unless sent manually.

facts.fact: Robocalls to landlines for market research or polling and for tax-exempt non-profit groups are permitted under FCC rules.
facts.quote: FCC rules allow market research or polling calls and calls on behalf of tax-exempt non-profit groups to landline numbers.

facts.fact: Emergency calls about danger to life, safety, or property are exempt from these robocall rules.
facts.quote: These rules do not apply to emergency calls about danger to life, safety, or property.

facts.fact: According to the FCC, the agency has issued hundreds of millions of dollars in enforcement actions against illegal robocallers.
facts.quote: Issued hundreds of millions of dollars in enforcement actions against illegal robocallers.

facts.fact: The FCC has mandated blocking of illegal international robocall traffic.
facts.quote: Mandated blocking of illegal international robocall traffic.

facts.fact: The FCC allowed phone companies to block numbers not on a customer's contact list (whitelist) when the customer opts in.
facts.quote: Allowed phone companies to block numbers not on a customer's contact list or "whitelist" when the customer opts in.

facts.fact: The FCC states that it does not resolve individual robocall complaints but uses them to guide policy and possible enforcement.
facts.quote: The FCC doesn’t resolve individual complaints but uses them to guide policy and possible enforcement under the Telephone Consumer Protection Act or the Truth in Caller ID Act.

facts.fact: Under the Telephone Consumer Protection Act and FCC rules, a robocall is a call made using an autodialer or a prerecorded or artificial voice message.
facts.quote: Robocalls are phone calls made using an autodialer or a prerecorded or artificial voice message.

facts.fact: Telephone solicitations are permissible with prior express permission or from tax-exempt non-profits.
facts.quote: Phone solicitations are permissible with prior express permission or from tax-exempt non-profits.

facts.fact: Telemarketing calls based on an established business relationship are not permitted to a landline without the consumer's advanced permission.
facts.quote: Telemarketing calls based on an established business relationship are not permitted to your landline phone without your advanced permission.

facts.fact: Telemarketers calling a home must provide their name along with the name, telephone number, and address where their employer or contractor can be contacted.
facts.quote: telemarketers calling your home must provide their name along with the name, telephone number, and address where their employer or contractor can be contacted.
